findings: April and November agree that Managed Payments is Stripe’s merchant-of-record product for digital goods via Checkout or Payment Links. Link is the buyer-facing identity from checkout through orders and transaction support, including “Sold through Link” and the LINK.COM* descriptor. The seller retains product support and can issue refunds and update subscriptions in Dashboard/API, subject to the specific payment-method exception. Stripe calculates/collects/files/remits covered indirect tax in more than 80 countries and withholds applicable tax on completion; outside its coverage the seller remains responsible and can use Stripe Tax to calculate tax at no additional charge. Old raw lines 8-34 and 62-87; new raw lines 9-42 and 64-91; mapped source lines 13-40.

Both document guest or Link-account checkout, guest onboarding for order management, configurable terms/privacy links, Link PDFs and receipt-setting independence, trial-start and longer-than-seven-day trial-end notices, standard renewal/card/failure controls, and Stripe-managed fraud rules/blocklists. An escalation goes to the configured support email; lack of merchant response within 48 hours can lead to a refund without approval. Stripe can refund within 60 days in certain cases; customer refunds include tax, with separate seller balance impact in certain jurisdictions. Old raw lines 23-58 and 64-87; new raw lines 23-60 and 66-91; source lines 19-46. The source’s table wording ‘seller escalated within 48h’ at line 22 misidentifies the clock despite its correct detailed rule at lines 35-37.

Both list tables conditioned on customer country, one-time versus recurring mode, local presentment and Adaptive Pricing support; default Adaptive Pricing does the presentment work when the method supports it. Konbini and WeChat Pay are prose examples of local payment methods and absent from both Managed Payments matrices. Neither general checkout text nor a method row guarantees that a method is displayed for a particular session or that payment succeeds. Old raw lines 27-29 and 89-114; new raw lines 27-29 and 103-128; source lines 54-72.

Both allow requested deletion across Managed Payments transactions and the associated Link account, cancel subscriptions sold through Managed Payments, remove customer information from related v2 Account, Customer, PaymentMethod, Invoice, PaymentIntent, Subscription and Charge objects including related merchant-side objects, and notify the seller by email on receipt of the request. That says customer data is deleted from relevant objects, with the notification tied to request receipt. Old raw lines 120-128; new raw lines 144-152; source lines 48-52.

Scoped implementation context identifies eligible products, Dashboard activation/development setup, and 2025-03-31.basil or later for the Checkout setup guide (companion set-up raw lines 11-16). The separate Payment Links guide assigns the API version floor to the Payment Links API and distinguishes the web Dashboard create path and iOS creation restriction (companion use-payment-links raw lines 16-36). The how-it-works comparison itself sets no new API-version floor. The distinct generic Klarna subscription and Bancontact generated-SEPA routes are scoped separately in wiki/concepts/stripe-klarna.md lines 14-27 and wiki/concepts/stripe-bancontact.md lines 12-20; the Managed Payments matrix controls its own route.
substantive_changes: New raw lines 31-36 explicitly disallow custom domains on Managed Payments checkouts, alongside continued support for custom terms and privacy links. Old raw lines 31-36 retained the links but did not address domains. Scope the limitation to these checkouts.

New raw lines 44-60 keep trial and renewal controls, but with Upcoming renewals disabled retain 6- and 12-month notices for Australia/UK and specify 12 months for all other countries. The April local-law wording and next-renewal cadence bullets are absent. November sets a 15-day default before anniversary, configurable in Dashboard › Subscription and email settings › Upcoming renewal events, with a minimum lead time of 7 days, without standard shorter timing options. With the setting on, Stripe sends before every renewal. Old raw lines 42-58 and source lines 42-46.

For subscriptions created by Managed Payments-enabled Checkout Sessions, November explicitly disallows direct API updates to subscription.default_payment_method and says customers can update it through the Customer Portal. This narrows the broad API subscription-update language without changing the seller’s product support or imposing a blanket subscription-update ban. Old raw lines 70-81; new raw lines 75-85; source lines 15-24 and 28-36.

April says Smart Disputes automatically submits evidence in most cases and a merchant can manually submit evidence (old raw line 19). November describes automated and manual evaluation, possible acceptance when Stripe expects to lose, evidence submitted by Stripe when countering without contacting the merchant for additional evidence, a dispute-received fee and potential charged dispute-prevention tooling, Stripe paying its own evidence-submission fee, and a merchant Dashboard accept/counter choice with an evidence fee when the merchant counters. Merchant-added but unsubmitted evidence can be reviewed and submitted by Stripe at no evidence-submission fee to the merchant. New raw lines 19-19 and 93-101; source line 24. This establishes workflow and fee distinctions without specifying fee amounts, prevalence or dispute outcomes.

Klarna country cell moves from Global to US, with one-time-only Managed Payments, required local presentment and no Adaptive Pricing unchanged. Optional withheld_tax identifies covered tax withheld/remitted; fee_net_of_withheld_tax shows processing fees excluding withheld tax. API access depends on available Stripe Reports fields and report versions, with no universal report schema implied. Old raw lines 116-118; new raw lines 130-142.

Ltd., or Stripe Payments Australia Pty Ltd. Maintain the affiliate role separately from Stripe as MoR and Link as the customer-facing identity; the guide does not map individual transactions, regions or accounts to an affiliate. reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/managed-payments/how-it-works, the April capture (old raw lines 8-40 and 42-128) and November capture (new raw lines 9-49 and 51-156) describe Managed Payments as Stripe's merchant-of-record solution for selling eligible digital products through Checkout or Payment Links without setting up local entities. Stripe handles covered indirect tax in more than 80 countries with applicable withholding on completed payment, manages fraud, disputes and transaction-level support, and leaves out-of-coverage tax compliance and product support with the seller. Link is the customer-facing identity, “Sold through Link”, with Link or guest checkout, local pricing by default subject to method support and presentment, the LINK.COM* descriptor, and receipts/invoices with PDFs from Link independently of Dashboard receipt settings. Guests need a Link account for Link order tools, and the merchant can separately offer Customer Portal or its own subscription management. Stripe can issue a discretionary refund after an unanswered 48-hour escalation or within 60 days in certain cases; refunds return customer tax, and some jurisdictions cause a corresponding merchant balance debit. A deletion request cancels Managed Payments subscriptions, removes customer data across the relevant Link/transaction objects including merchant-side v2 Account, Customer, PaymentMethod, Invoice, PaymentIntent, Subscription and Charge, and prompts an email to the merchant when received. November adds Checkout custom-domain and subscription payment-method constraints, changes method eligibility and renewal reminders, details disputes, report fields and Stripe acquiring affiliates, and preserves the underlying support identity and tax boundaries. Companion setup instructions establish eligibility, Dashboard activation and API 2025-03-31.basil or later for the Checkout build path, with a separately scoped Payment Links API floor. source-stripe-managed-payments-how-it-works.md preserves much of the April operating model but its dispute, renewal and method rows need dated corrections, its short 48-hour row is misleading despite the fuller rule, and it lacks the November additions.

In November’s documented dispute workflow, Stripe uses automated tools and manual review, can accept if it expects the seller is unlikely to win, and submits evidence without requesting more from the seller when it decides to counter. A received dispute incurs a separate dispute-received fee. Stripe charges the merchant account separately for enabled prevention tools. Stripe covers the evidence-submission fee whenever it submits evidence to counter, including when it chooses to submit evidence the merchant only added in the Dashboard. Adding evidence without submitting it leaves Stripe to review and possibly submit. A merchant countering the dispute directly in the Dashboard incurs the evidence-submission fee. New raw lines 93-101 give these responsibilities. Keep reciprocal dated warnings for April’s Smart Disputes automatic evidence for most disputes, global Klarna and recurring Belgium Bancontact. November describes US-only Klarna and Belgium Bancontact, each for one-time payments in Managed Payments. With Dashboard Upcoming renewals enabled, Stripe sends an email before every renewal. With it disabled, Stripe still sends anniversary emails before the 6- and 12-month anniversaries in Australia and the United Kingdom and before the 12-month anniversary elsewhere. The default lead time is 15 days, configurable via Dashboard Subscription and email settings › Upcoming renewal events with a minimum of 7 days. Shorter standard renewal-reminder timing options do not apply. New raw lines 51-60 support these branches. Correct source line 42’s “Mandatory Regardless of Dashboard Setting” heading, and preserve April’s enabled branch and the dated disabled branch with its local-law wording and overlapping 30-day and 7-day cadence bullets (old raw lines 49-58). Source line 46 independently reverses April’s “less frequently than monthly” condition. In the Balance Change from Activity Report, Payout Reconciliation Report, and Ending Balance Reconciliation Report, the default `fee` column combines Stripe fees and withheld tax. Optional `withheld_tax` identifies indirect tax Stripe withheld and remitted on the merchant’s behalf, and `fee_net_of_withheld_tax` shows Stripe processing fees excluding withheld tax. API availability depends on the fields and report versions available in Stripe Reports. These accounting rules are in new raw lines 130-142. The November direct API restriction on subscription.default_payment_method is scoped to subscriptions created by Managed Payments-enabled Checkout Sessions, with the Customer Portal available to the customer and other seller update abilities retained. Custom terms and privacy links coexist with the Managed Payments checkout custom-domain restriction. The acquiring affiliate list identifies possible processors without account assignment. Method configuration and local presentment govern visibility, while the captures give no account-specific availability or payment or dispute outcome guarantee. Image path, emphasis, table layout, the Afterpay label on the same URL, headings, and unchanged setup links change presentation or navigation. The captures establish neither legal timing changes nor Smart Disputes deprecation.
